condition: IgA vasculitis (Henoch–Schönlein purpura) with abdominal pain
permutationLabel: 6-year-old, purpura, arthralgia, colicky pain and nephritis (base case)
summary: 6-year-old boy (21 kg) a week after a sore throat: palpable purpura on buttocks and legs, painful swollen ankles, 2 days of colicky periumbilical pain with one dark-blood stool; urine blood 2+, protein 1+. Risk of intussusception and nephritis; not an appendicectomy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Tummy pain and a rash on the legs
inputs.hpi: Sore throat 1 week ago. Four days ago a raised red-purple rash appeared on his buttocks and legs, then painful swollen ankles. Two days of colicky pain around the belly button, vomited once, one stool with dark blood this morning. No fever now.

exam.skin: Palpable non-blanching purpura over buttocks, posterior thighs and lower legs; no truncal rash.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild periumbilical tenderness, no mass, no guarding.
exam.msk: Both ankles swollen and tender, full range.

inputs.socialHistory: Primary school; immunisations up to date.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: IgA vasculitis (Henoch–Schönlein purpura) with gastrointestinal and renal involvement
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: IgA vasculitis (palpable purpura, arthritis, abdominal pain, haematuria/proteinuria; normal platelets). Abdominal ultrasound to exclude intussusception; urine protein:creatinine ratio and BP; paediatric team; urinalysis follow-up for nephritis.

socratesAnswers.associated: Vomiting once, blood in stool, rash, joint pain

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE has no IgA vasculitis (HSP) disease node (pane-engine has 130 diseases, none for IgA vasculitis (HSP)); top 3: appendicitis, inguinal hernia, cholecystitis. Symptom inference ranks Henoch-Schönlein purpura #1 (secondary view).
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add IgA vasculitis (D69.0) as a PANE node/protocol: ultrasound for severe pain (intussusception), urinalysis/BP follow-up, no surgery.

mustInclude.note: Colicky pain with blood per rectum in IgA vasculitis: exclude (usually ileo-ileal) intussusception.

mustExclude.note: Weight 21 kg. Paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g, co-amoxiclav 1.2 g, meropenem 1 g, morphine 2.5–5 mg, ondansetron 4 mg and fixed 1 L, 1–2 L or 500 mL fluid volumes are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg, mL/kg) dosing. Prescribing accuracy is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
Abdominal pain of IgA vasculitis: an appendicectomy plan is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: SHARE initiative — European consensus recommendations for IgA vasculitis (Henoch–Schönlein purpura)
guideline.section: Urinalysis and blood pressure at presentation and during follow-up (nephritis); abdominal ultrasound for severe abdominal pain to exclude intussusception; corticosteroids may be considered for severe abdominal pain
guideline.citation: Ozen S, Marks SD, Brogan P, et al. European consensus-based recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of immunoglobulin A vasculitis — the SHARE initiative. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2019;58:1607–1616.

guideline.name: EULAR/PRINTO/PRES classification criteria — Henoch–Schönlein purpura
guideline.section: Purpura or petechiae (lower-limb predominance) plus ≥ 1 of: abdominal pain, histopathology with IgA deposition, arthritis/arthralgia, renal involvement
guideline.citation: Ozen S, Pistorio A, Iusan SM, et al. EULAR/PRINTO/PRES criteria for Henoch–Schönlein purpura, childhood polyarteritis nodosa, childhood Wegener granulomatosis and childhood Takayasu arteritis. Ann Rheum Dis. 2010;69:798–806.

rationale: Abdominal pain can precede or accompany the rash of IgA vasculitis; the surgical questions are intussusception (ultrasound) and avoiding a negative laparotomy, while the long-term risk is nephritis (urinalysis and BP).
